articles.title: Nvidia, AI Industry Face Prospect of Future Without Huang
articles.description: Bloomberg's Emily Chang said that while Nvidia will survive the ouster of CEO Jensen Huang, questions remain about if it will be able to thrive in the same way without Huang's relationships with global leaders and no predetermined successor. Chang said the national security implications around the company are in the spotlight going forward, as Colette Kress, the interim CEO in the wake of Huang's resignation, also believes that Nvidia should be able to sell the most advanced chips to China. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: 'Essential' That US Upholds Export Controls on Chips, Says Ben Buchanan
articles.description: Ben Buchanan, former White House special advisor for Artificial Intelligence in the Biden Administration and author of the new book 'The Bitter Struggle: Superintelligence, Superpowers, and the Fate of the World,' said that it is 'essential' that the US maintain its curbs around exports of US chips to China and is 'more urgent now' given the lead the US has in the AI race. Buchanan said that the Trump administration made a mistake in not enforcing the Biden administration's 'diffusion rule,' which extended strict controls on AI chip exports to stop chips from reaching adversaries. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Huang Affair Suggests 'Compromised Objectivity' Says Anna Ashton
articles.description: Anna Ashton, founder of Ashton Analytics and former China analyst at the Department of Defense, said that it doesn't matter if Alice Huang was an unwitting participant or a spy for the Chinese government because she already worked for Megaspeed, a company that was 'seriously distrusted' for attempting to work around US export controls on chips. Ashton said that Jensen Huang's affair with Alice Huang suggests 'massively compromised objectivity' on the part of the former Nvidia CEO. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Courts Should Employ a Simpler Fair Use Analysis for Noncompeting Criticism
articles.description: Copyright and trademark rights act in tension with the First Amendment. Indeed, “unlike other property rights, [these] are a form of content-based, government-imposed speech restriction.” (Mark Lemley and Eugene Volokh, Freedom of Speech and Injunctions in Intellectual Property Cases, 48 Duke L.J. 147, 206 (1998)). As such, courts have determined that criticism, generally, puts the critic beyond the reach of a copyright or trademark claim.
